chunks: Abu ʿAli al-Ashʿari, from Muhammad ibn Salim, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from ʿAmr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abi Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: “O assembly of people, I must not find a man whose deceased died at night and he waited with him until morning, nor a man whose deceased died by day and he waited with him until night. Do not wait with your dead for the rising of the sun nor for its setting. Hasten them to their resting places. May Allah, Exalted is He, have mercy on you.”
The people said: “And you too, O Messenger of Allah, may Allah have mercy on you.”

key_terms.مَضَاجِعِهِمْ: their resting places, meaning their graves

ai.seo_question: Should the burial of the deceased be delayed until morning or evening in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith instructs that burial of the deceased should not be unnecessarily delayed from night until morning or from day until night. It emphasizes hastening the dead to their graves as part of proper conduct toward the deceased and as a Prophetic sunnah (prophetic tradition).
